headline: Red Sox look to bounce back against Royals after Seattle heartbreaker
morning_brew: I watched that final drive in Seattle through my fingers like a horror movie and the result was just as painful. Drake Maye had a long night at the office, and the team just couldn't find the necessary spark in those final quarters to swing it our way. Losing by a slim margin of 13-10 when every possession feels like a turning point takes about three years off my life, but that is the brutal nature of the beast in this league.

Back at Fenway, the Red Sox are looking to shake off a frustrating 6-4 loss to the Angels where the starting pitching just didn't have the command we needed in the early frames. Watching the bullpen come in and hold the line was a silver lining, but when you put yourself in a hole that deep against an opponent, the comeback attempt always feels like an uphill climb. We are currently sitting in position for a wild card spot, so every single night at the park is massive for keeping the Duck Boat fund from being frozen pending investigation.

We have no time to mope around with a series against the Royals starting tonight at the oldest yard in baseball. I am looking for the bats to wake up and for the rotation to settle in early because we need to stack some wins before we hit the road again. I will be glued to the screen and hoping for a cleaner game, because my neighbor Rick has already started a new investigation into why we struggle against teams below us in the standings, and I really do not need to hear his theories on the bullpen while I am trying to eat my dinner.
